newsitem.title: JAPAN: Goods and services surplus won't rise greatly--MOF.
newsitem.headline: Goods and services surplus won't rise greatly--MOF.

text.p: Japan's surplus in goods and services is unlikely to increase significantly as a trend, although it may fluctuate in the short term, a Ministry of Finance (MOF) official told reporters on Wednesday.

"Due to structural changes in the Japanese economy, the surplus in goods and services is unlikely to increase significantly as a trend, although there may be fluctuations in the short term," the official said.
He also said the rise in Japan's consumption tax in April was one factor behind a jump in the current account surplus for May.
He said imports to Japan, including cars, fell sharply after the tax increase, while Japanese firms boosted exports.
Japan raised its national consumption tax to five percent from three percent on April 1.
The measure was preceded by an increase in domestic private consumption and followed by a drop in reaction.
Japanese manufacturers are widely believed to have increased exports after April to make up for the drop in domestic consumption.
